answer: At the nadir of a bad epoch, a flood of fresh identities is most dangerous, so cap admissions: each epoch only a fixed number of new-identity slots open, filled by a lottery over deposits. Like a lantern rationed to a few hands, a sybil farm holding 1,000 tickets still wins slots in proportion to its share, and every losing ticket costs a forfeited deposit. Winners earn at a sonnet-like steady pace, so scaling is slow and costly.
